key_insight: Generative LLMs can evaluate ASR outputs more semantically faithfully than WER by (1) choosing better hypotheses, (2) producing generative embeddings for semantic distance, and (3) providing qualitative error classifications that align better with human judgment.
problem_solved: Traditional WER is insensitive to meaning and often fails to reflect perceived transcription quality; the paper explores whether decoder-based generative LLMs can provide evaluation signals that capture semantic correctness and human preferences.
method: Pairwise selection: use a generative LLM to choose the better transcript between two ASR hypotheses.
Generative-embedding distance: derive embeddings from the LLM’s generative process to compute semantic distance between reference and hypothesis.
Qualitative classification: prompt the LLM to produce qualitative/error-type labels and explanations to characterize ASR mistakes beyond word-level edits.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with more human-aligned, semantic evaluation tools for ASR, enabling better model comparison, tuning, and downstream-task relevance than WER alone.
visual_elements: Side-by-side example: two ASR hypotheses + LLM verdict (pairwise selection) with a short explanation.
Bar chart comparing correlation with human judgments: WER vs embedding-based vs LLM-based metrics.
Pipeline diagram: audio → ASR → multiple hypotheses → LLM evaluator (pairwise / embeddings / qualitative) → score/labels.
Error taxonomy visualization: pie/stacked chart of qualitative error classes produced by the LLM (e.g., semantic error, omission, insertion, punctuation/formatting).
paper_title: Evaluation of Automatic Speech Recognition Using Generative Large Language Models
paper_authors: Thibault Bañeras-Roux, Shashi Kumar, Driss Khalil, Sergio Burdisso, Petr Motlicek
